fatal_errors: The response addresses AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA rather than equimolar WTaTiVZr refractory HEA.
It uses duplex stainless steel 2205 rather than commercially used pure tungsten as the baseline.
It analyzes aqueous tribocorrosion and thermal shock rather than high-temperature mechanical strength, plastic strain, brittle-to-ductile behavior, and fracture toughness.

The proposed passivation and wear mechanism is unrelated to the target solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, dislocation behavior, grain-boundary cohesion, and crack-impedance interpretation.
None of the target compression, temperature-dependent indentation, or scratch-toughness conditions and outcomes are reconstructed.
No supporting prior evidence is cited, and the falsification rule is generic rather than tied to a causal controlled comparison.
explanation: The generated hypothesis is about a different alloy system, comparator, loading mode, environment, mechanism, and outcome. Although it states explicit operating boundaries and proposes several measurable tribocorrosion observables, those tests cannot answer the requested WTaTiVZr-versus-tungsten question. It misses the target observations of approximately 1.6 GPa room-temperature yield strength, about 6% plastic strain, strength retention to 500 °C, disappearance of indentation cracking above 200 °C, and roughly 38 versus 25 MPa√m scratch-derived toughness. A relevant discriminating experiment would compare identically prepared WTaTiVZr and tungsten under matched compression or indentation conditions while characterizing the two-BCC-phase dendritic segregation and crack/dislocation behavior; the proposed experiment does not do so.
